content:
The highly anticipated 'Ted Lasso' has finally returned, with the first episode of the show's fourth season now available for subscribers to watch on Apple TV+.

Ted Lasso is finally back

More than three years after the third season finale aired, the first episode of the fourth season is now streaming on Apple TV+ for viewers to watch.

Apple is heavily promoting the show's return this time, including arranging for Jason Sudeikis and Brendan Hunt, who play coach Ted and Beard respectively, to make surprise appearances during the World Cup final, and will hold a lookalike competition at the Apple Fifth Avenue Plaza in New York this Thursday (August 6).

If you've managed to avoid all spoilers about the show's return and want to keep it that way, it's recommended that you skip straight to the main point and go watch the first episode right away. But if you don't mind getting a rough idea of this season's direction in advance, here's a synopsis of the new season provided by Apple TV+:

The fourth season of 'Ted Lasso' has a total of 10 episodes and will air until October 7, 2026, and is expected to be the first of a new three-season run.

Most of the main cast will return, with new additions including Tanya Reynolds (who appeared in 'Underdogs') and Paloma Cinco (who appeared in 'De La Cruz'), the latter being Cristo Fernandez's biological sister. Cristo Fernandez plays the fan-favorite Dani Rojas in the show, and has since transitioned to becoming a professional footballer.

Check out the trailer for the new season of 'Ted Lasso' below:

Apple TV+ costs $12.99 per month and is also included in the Apple One subscription bundle. The platform has a number of popular shows and movies, such as 'Severance', 'The Studio', 'The Morning Show', 'Shrinking' and 'Silo'.
